## Refined Questions and Analysis Choices

#Central Question: 
- What is the relationship between temporal / land cover factors and fast fire events (high mean growth rate per event)

#Supporting Questions: 
- What is the relationship between temporal / land cover factors and the longest fire events (duration).
- Is there a relationship between land cover and maximum, mean, minimum daily fire growth per event.


# Observations and Variables
There are a total of 4329 observations (fire events) available to use

Variable: ig_month 
Description: The month of the earliest date contained in the event

Variable: ig_year
Description: The year of the earliest date contained in the event.

Variable: fsr_km2_dy
Description: Total kilometers burned for the entire event divided by the duration of the fire event. (***use this as response variable for central question???)

Variable: event_dur
Description: Duration of the event in days

Variable: mx_grw_km2
Description: Maximum daily fire growth per event in square kilometers

Variable: mn_grw_km2
Description: Minimum daily fire growth per event in square kilometers

Variable: mu_grw_km2
Description: Mean daily fire growth per event in square kilometers

Variable: lc_name
Description: Character string of the landcover type from the year before the fire. 

# Intended Comparison / Unresolved Data Limitations
An intended comparison is the central question and first supporting question. Addressing whether the temporal / land factors are contributing more to the growth rate of the fire events or the duration of the fire event.

There are no unresolved data limitations, since there are no gaps for the intended variables.

### What is the relationship between time of year and which land cover types see the fastest fires?

### Response variable: mean growth; Predictors: land cover, month, year

```{r - time of year, land cover type, mean growth two-way ANOVA}
# Group data
mean_growth_group <- california_events_processed %>%
  group_by(lc_name, ig_month, ig_year) %>%
  summarise(mean_growth_rate = mean(mu_grw_km2))

#viewing the grouped data frame and commenting it out after
#view(mean_growth_group)

# create new data frame of just question variables
mean_growth <- california_events_processed %>%
  select(lc_name, ig_month, ig_year, mu_grw_km2)

#viewing the data frame of variables and commenting it out after
#view(mean_growth)

# Format as aov
mean_growth_aov2 <- aov(data = mean_growth, mu_grw_km2 ~ ig_month + lc_name)
summary(mean_growth_aov2)

# Format as lm
mean_growth_anova_2way2 <- lm(data = mean_growth, mu_grw_km2 ~ ig_month + lc_name)
summary(mean_growth_anova_2way2)

# Run a post-hoc test for pairwise differences
TukeyHSD(mean_growth_aov2)

```

# Figures
```{r - figures}
#Plot of mean growth for each land cover class and month
mean_growth_anova_plot <- ggplot(mean_growth, aes(y = mu_grw_km2, x = ig_month, color = lc_name)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size= 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Mean Growth of Wildfires across Land Use Classes and Months",
       x= "Month",
       y="Mean Growth (km2)") 

mean_growth_anova_plot

#Plot of mean growth for each month separated by land cover class
mean_growth_anova_plot_separate <- ggplot(mean_growth, aes(y = mu_grw_km2, x = ig_month, color = lc_name)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size= 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(vars(lc_name)) +
  labs(title = "Mean Growth of Wildfires across Land Use Classes and Months",
       x= "Month",
       y="Mean Growth (km2)") 

mean_growth_anova_plot_separate
```

# Initial Analytical Application
## Mean Growth
To begin to understand if there is a relationship between time of year and which land cover types experience the fastest fires, we completed a two way ANOVA as well as Tukey's Honest Significant Differences. We also created two scatterplots to visualize these relationships, one with all land cover classes combined and one with them separated. The two way ANOVA indicated significance for the following land cover classes: Closed Shrublands (0.000000000247), Evergreen Needleleaf Forests (0.0000053), Grasslands (0.0000163), Open Shrublands (0.0000000128), Woody Savannas (0.000894), Savannas (0.002197), and Evergreen Broadleaf Forests (0.045657), as well as the following months: August (0.001385), July (0.031237), and October (0.019439). These results can also visually be seen seen in the scatterplots.
